# Target
Worktree `/Users/bnjoroge/preloop-gh-app-api-compat`. Files (ONLY these): `crates/preloop-runner-server/src/openapi.rs`, `crates/preloop-runner-server/src/dispatch_tests.rs`. Do NOT touch dispatch.rs, github.rs, broker.rs, routes.rs, errors.rs, runs.rs, github_app.rs, or docs.

# Change (three validated items)
1. **ApiErrorResponse schema mismatch (contract)** — openapi.rs line ~15: `ApiErrorResponse { pub message: String }` but the real native error body is `{ "error": <message> }` (errors.rs `impl IntoResponse for ApiError`). Change the schema field name to `error` (update the doc comment accordingly: "Human-readable error message" stays). This is used by `body = ApiErrorResponse` on many routes — the field rename applies everywhere automatically.
2. **Missing documented responses (contract)** — add to the four dispatch operations' `responses(...)` lists: `(status = 502, description = "Failed to fetch workflows or resolve the ref", body = ApiErrorResponse)` for `workflow_dispatch_trigger`, `repository_dispatch_trigger`, `list_dispatch_workflows`, and `list_dispatch_runs` (all four can return bad_gateway); and `(status = 403, description = "No repository access", body = ApiErrorResponse)` for the two READ ops only (`list_dispatch_workflows`, `list_dispatch_runs` — authorize_read 403s; the POST ops already document 403 with their permission-specific description). Insert keeping the existing status ordering (e.g. 204,400,401,403,404,409,422 + 502; reads: 200?,401,403,404,502 — check each op's current list and insert consistently, 502 last).
3. **dispatch_tests.rs test organization + coverage (tests)** — (a) Move the misplaced `M3: third-party installation tokens` section header (currently ~line 906, immediately followed by the `M4: multi-App registry` header with no tests between) down to directly precede the third-party installation-token tests (which live ~line 1119-1275); keep the `M4` header at its current position before the registry tests. (b) Add two tests for `resolve_dispatch_ref` tag paths in dispatch.rs: one dispatching to an explicit `refs/tags/<name>` ref and one to a bare tag name (`ref` field = tag name) on a tag created in the fixture git repo (`init_git_repo` creates a repo — create a tag with `git tag` in the fixture workspace before dispatching; follow the existing fixture helpers like `git_ok`/`init_git_repo` in dispatch_tests.rs and the existing workflow_dispatch test pattern ~line 300-360, using a workflow file that is `workflow_dispatch`-triggered; assert 204 + the run recorded with the tag ref). Preserve the existing unknown-ref assertion test. (c) Add a read-endpoint authorization test: `record_ledger_token` (fixture helper, ~line 182) with a token scoped to a DIFFERENT repository (e.g. `other/repo`) while dispatching a GET to `/repos/octocat/repo/actions/workflows` and `/repos/octocat/repo/actions/runs` — assert 403 (authorize_read). Follow the existing ledger-test pattern (`dispatch_with_own_minted_token_authenticates_offline_via_ledger` ~line 815 uses record_ledger_token + pin_api_base) — pin the API base with `pin_api_base("http://127.0.0.1:1")` where the fixture needs it; note GET helpers: check whether the tests file has a GET helper or only post_json — if only post_json exists, use the same `app` router with `axum::body::Body`/`Request` like post_json does (read post_json's implementation and mirror it for GET).

# Acceptance
- Compile-read coherent; utoipa attribute syntax valid; new tests follow existing fixture patterns exactly (no new deps, no new files).
- Report per item: exact changes, new test names.

changes: ApiErrorResponse schema field renamed `pub message: String` → `pub error: String` (line 16); doc comment `/// Human-readable error message.` retained unchanged. Applies to every `body = ApiErrorResponse` route since they reference the schema type.

Added `(status = 502, description = "Failed to fetch workflows or resolve the ref", body = ApiErrorResponse)` to all four dispatch ops, last in each responses list (after 422 for the two POSTs, after 404 for the two GETs).
Added `(status = 403, description = "No repository access", body = ApiErrorResponse)` to the two READ ops only, inserted after 401 and before 404 to preserve status ordering.

Final lists: workflow_dispatch_trigger: 204,400,401,403,404,409,422,502; repository_dispatch_trigger: 204,400,401,403,404,422,502; list_dispatch_workflows: 200,401,403,404,502; list_dispatch_runs: 200,401,403,404,502. POST ops' existing 403 (permission-specific descriptions) untouched.

(a) M3 header `// ─── M3: third-party installation tokens (stubbed github.com) ───` moved from old line ~906 (where it sat directly above the M4 header with no tests between) to directly precede `third_party_installation_token_dispatches_when_it_holds_actions_write`; M4 header stays at its position before `two_app_registry`.

(b) Two new tests after `workflow_dispatch_unknown_ref_is_404` (which is preserved unchanged): `workflow_dispatch_to_explicit_tag_ref_is_204` (POSTs `"ref": "refs/tags/v1.0"`) and `workflow_dispatch_bare_tag_name_is_204` (POSTs `"ref": "v1.0"`, bare name — branch-first-then-tag). Both create a lightweight tag `v1.0` on the fixture's initial commit via `git_ok(&temp.path().join("ws"), &["tag", "v1.0"])` after `dispatch_fixture`, dispatch a `workflow_dispatch`-triggered workflow (DISPATCH_WORKFLOW) with `inputs.greeting`, and assert 204 + exactly one run with `submission.git_ref == "refs/tags/v1.0"`, `github.event.ref == "refs/tags/v1.0"`, `github.event.ref_type == "tag"`, `head_sha.len() == 40`.

(c) New test `read_endpoints_reject_ledger_token_scoped_to_another_repo` after `ledger_token_scoped_to_another_repo_is_403`: `dispatch_fixture_with_app` + `record_ledger_token(state, "ghs_other_repo_read_token", "other/repo", &[("actions", "write")])` + `pin_api_base("http://127.0.0.1:1")`, then GETs `/repos/octocat/repo/actions/workflows` and `/repos/octocat/repo/actions/runs` via the existing `get_json` helper — both assert 403 (authorize_read).

Verified against dispatch.rs/github.rs (read-only): tag refs resolve in the local workspace via `git rev-parse`/`ls-tree`/`git show`; `resolve_dispatch_ref` returns ("refs/tags/<name>", "tag") for both explicit-prefixed and bare tag names; the payload ref/ref_type flow verbatim into `submission.git_ref` and `github.event`.
